def-emg-fx-maxwell-presymplectic-current.oldParagraph: There is a unique smooth real function $u_{\alpha,\beta}$ on $\Sigma$ such that $\iota_\Sigma^*\omega_g(\alpha,\beta)=u_{\alpha,\beta}\,\mathrm{vol}_\gamma$. Define the pairing $\Omega_\Sigma(\alpha,\beta)$ precisely when $u_{\alpha,\beta}\in L^1(\Sigma,\mu_\gamma)$, meaning $\int_\Sigma|u_{\alpha,\beta}|\,d\mu_\gamma<\infty$, and then set $\Omega_\Sigma(\alpha,\beta):=\int_\Sigma u_{\alpha,\beta}\,d\mu_\gamma$. This absolute-integrability condition is the convergence convention on noncompact $\Sigma$ and makes the value independent of any exhaustion or ordering. In length coordinates on $\Sigma$, the coefficients of $d\alpha$ and $d\beta$ have units $\mathrm m^{-2}$, those of $\omega_g$ have units $\mathrm m^{-3}$, $u_{\alpha,\beta}$ is dimensionless, and $d\mu_\gamma$ has volume units $\mathrm m^3$; thus the normalized integral is dimensionless. Replacing normalized variations by physical-potential variations $\kappa_0\alpha$ and $\kappa_0\beta$ multiplies the current by $\kappa_0^2$; an action prefactor is not fixed here.

cex-emg-fx-cfl-discrete-growth.oldProof1.1: 1.1 The matrices in [A1] are the signed boundary-incidence maps of one oriented tetrahedron, with edges ordered $01,02,03,12,13,23$, faces ordered $012,013,023,123$, and cell orientation $0123$. Matrix multiplication gives $D_1D_0=0_{4\times4}$ and $D_2D_1=0_{1\times6}$. Also $D_2x=-1+1=0$ and $D_0^{\mathsf T}d_{1/2}=0_{1\times1}$, so the initial state satisfies both constraints. [given, F1, A1, algebra]
